worldPv.title: Global Implementation of Balcony Solar
worldPv.lead: A framework view tracking how plug-in PV is expanding through lived experience: German legal reforms, Western legislation, and African off-grid implementations (Demo).

map.legendLegalPlug: 800W plug certified (DE, UK, EU states) — outlet-direct on 230V grids
map.legendPlugExemption: 1,200W waiver (UT, CA, etc.) — interconnect study waived for high-load homes
map.legendAppliance: 600W notice / urban BIPV (AT, SG, etc.) — appliance class & building-integrated
map.legendStorage: No export / storage self-supply (JP, CN, TW, VN, etc.) — grid-defense storage only
map.legendStrictCode: No outlet tie / licensed work (US conservative states) — NEC-compliant electrical work
map.legendProductiveOffgrid: Agri & cold-chain infra (East Africa, etc.) — solar pumping & cold storage
map.legendMicroSolarKit: Life kits / PayGo (Rwanda, Uganda, etc.) — pay-as-you-go lighting & recycled batteries

legendGroupDesc.grid_no_plug: Grid exists but reverse-flow defense and licensed work force storage self-supply
legendGroupDesc.no_grid_leapfrog: Weak/absent grids where agri pumps and PayGo life kits lead
legendGroupDesc.grid_tied: Markets with authorized plug-in and export/netting on the grid
legendGroupDesc.offgrid_bop: Weak/absent grids where agri pumps and PayGo life kits lead

modelFilter.productive_offgrid: 🟣 Agri & cold-chain infra (solar pumps / cold storage · East Africa)

outlet.plugOk: 🟢 No construction (just plug into an outlet)
outlet.necStrict: 🔴 Licensed electrical work required (no DIY outlet tie)

excess.selfConsume: △ Use it at home first (export credit small or out of scope)
excess.batteryNight: — Charge a battery and use it at night

germany.name: Germany
germany.procedure: Registration only (simple online notice → same-day use)
germany.ruleSummary: Certified up to 800W. Online registration alone completes the filing.
germany.meterRequirement: Legacy reverse-spin temporarily allowed (smart meters rolling out)
germany.windSafety: Stow inside railing in high wind (flush clamps recommended)
germany.summary: Grid connection with Federal Network Agency registration only. Tenant install rights are law; adoption exceeds 1 million households.

austria.name: Austria
austria.incentives: Local environmental grants in some municipalities
austria.mountingRules: No-drill railing fix (appliance class; electrician not required)
austria.summary: Classed as a small appliance. A 2-week prior notice to the grid operator is enough for easy plug-in operation.

switzerland.name: Switzerland
switzerland.meterRequirement: Prior notice to the utility required
switzerland.windSafety: Snow load and Alpine wind resistance needed
switzerland.mountingRules: Outside-railing install needs written landlord consent
switzerland.summary: Plug-in allowed up to 600W rated. Inside the railing is freer; outside mounts need property-manager consent.

uk.name: United Kingdom (UK)
uk.procedure: Registration only (simple online notice → same-day use)
uk.antiIslanding: ENA G98 certified (stop within 0.5s on unplug)
uk.meterRequirement: Smart meter recommended (notify ENA within 28 days)
uk.windSafety: Coastal sites: 30 m/s wind rating or stow
uk.mountingRules: BS 1363 (fused 5A plug required; outdoor IP outlet)
uk.summary: With a fused 5A plug, up to 800W grid-tie via post-install notice to ENA within 28 days.

france.name: France
france.windSafety: Flatten or stow when high-wind warnings
france.summary: Free online CACSI filing to Enedis enables same-day use. DIY kits are widely sold at home centers.

italy.name: Italy
italy.meterRequirement: Bidirectional smart meter (≤350W needs no filing)
italy.windSafety: Mediterranean gusts: fixed or fold-away stow
italy.mountingRules: Railing clamps OK outside protected streetscape zones
italy.summary: Under ARERA rules, ≤350W needs no procedure. 350–800W is authorized via a simplified notice.

belgium.name: Belgium
belgium.meterRequirement: Digital smart meter required (no disc reverse-spin)
belgium.summary: To prevent reverse spin on legacy disc meters, plug-in grid-tie is allowed only in homes with digital meters.

usa.name: United States
usa.paybackYears: Depends on state rules (3 years to hard to recover)
usa.baseLoadCoverage: Daytime base load to outage backup, by state model
usa.incentives: Federal ITC and state rebates vary widely
usa.meterRequirement: Depends on utility and state rules
usa.mountingRules: HOA and building codes differ sharply by city/state
usa.summary: Federal electrical-code rules set the baseline, but Utah’s 1,200W waiver and California’s permit exemption plus storage pairing show how state rules drive implementation. Open child pins for state detail.

us-ut.name: Utah
us-ut.tenantRights: State plug-in allowance (HOA may still apply)
us-ut.incentives: Federal ITC stacking depends on gear and install type
us-ut.meterRequirement: Full interconnect/application waiver within the cap
us-ut.mountingRules: Railing clamps preferred; drilling needs lease rules check
us-ut.summary: 2025 statute fully waives interconnection study up to 1,200W—the most plug-in-friendly U.S. state.

us-ca.name: California
us-ca.baseLoadCoverage: Partial self-supply including evening peak via storage
us-ca.windSafety: Coastal wind and wildfire-smoke inspection recommended
us-ca.mountingRules: Balcony installs follow city and HOA ordinances
us-ca.ruleSummary: Permit-exempt up to 1,200W. Low export rates make storage pairing mainstream.
us-ca.summary: Permit exemption advances 1,200W-class balcony PV while low export rates make storage self-consumption mainstream.

us-co.name: Colorado
us-co.tenantRights: State plug-in allowance (HOA may still apply)
us-co.incentives: Federal ITC and community renewables grants (capped)
us-co.meterRequirement: Interconnection study waived within the cap
us-co.windSafety: High-altitude gusts and snow load: clamp strength required
us-co.mountingRules: Railing clamps preferred; check HOA rules
us-co.summary: Adopted Utah’s 1,200W waiver template and is expanding plug-in installs around decarbonized community autonomy.

us-wa.name: Washington
us-wa.tenantRights: State plug-in allowance (HOA may still apply)
us-wa.incentives: State renewables rights plus federal ITC
us-wa.meterRequirement: Interconnection study waived within the cap
us-wa.windSafety: Coastal wind: secure mounting check required
us-wa.mountingRules: Railing clamps preferred; check lease rules
us-wa.summary: Introduced a 1,200W waiver as part of expanding renewables rights—one of the West Coast states following Utah.

us-or.name: Oregon
us-or.tenantRights: State plug-in allowance (HOA may still apply)
us-or.meterRequirement: Interconnection study waived within the cap
us-or.mountingRules: Railing clamps preferred; check lease rules
us-or.summary: Advancing a 1,200W waiver as part of West Coast plug-in legalization—another Utah-template follower.

us-az.name: Arizona
us-az.tenantRights: State plug-in allowance (HOA may still apply)
us-az.incentives: Federal ITC plus strong peak-rate avoidance
us-az.meterRequirement: Interconnection study waived within the cap
us-az.mountingRules: Railing clamps preferred; check HOA aesthetics rules
us-az.summary: Pushing household self-supply on top-tier U.S. insolation; adopted a Utah-style 1,200W plug-in waiver.

us-me.name: Maine
us-me.tenantRights: State plug-in allowance (HOA may still apply)
us-me.incentives: State renewables grants and federal ITC
us-me.meterRequirement: Interconnection study waived within the cap
us-me.windSafety: Coastal storms and snow load resistance required
us-me.mountingRules: Railing clamps preferred; winter stow recommended
us-me.summary: An early Northeast adopter of permitting waivers—Utah’s model recognized on the East Coast.

us-mn.name: Minnesota
us-mn.incentives: State distributed EMS programs and federal ITC
us-mn.meterRequirement: Interconnection study waived within the cap
us-mn.mountingRules: Railing clamps preferred; keep snow clearance
us-mn.summary: Adopted a 1,200W plug-in waiver as part of cold-climate distributed EMS—Midwest follower of Utah’s model.

us-tx.name: Texas
us-tx.paybackYears: Hard to recover (outage self-supply is the goal)
us-tx.incentives: Federal ITC mainly tied to rooftop interconnect
us-tx.mountingRules: Outlet plug-in not recognized / HOA limits
us-tx.summary: ERCOT rules and NEC 690 keep outlet plug-in unrecognized. Off-grid storage is the practical path for freeze/heat grid outages.

us-fl.name: Florida
us-fl.incentives: Federal ITC mainly tied to rooftop interconnect
us-fl.windSafety: Hurricane regions: rigid wind and stow rules
us-fl.mountingRules: Outlet plug-in treated as illegal wiring / HOA limits
us-fl.summary: NEC 690 plus utility pressure (e.g. FPL) and high-margin sales loans remain. Outlet plug-in is effectively impractical.

us-ny.name: New York
us-ny.tenantRights: Lease / co-op approval is a barrier
us-ny.paybackYears: Hard to recover (process cost is high)
us-ny.incentives: State/city renewables grants focus on rooftop interconnect
us-ny.meterRequirement: Grid interconnect processes often run long
us-ny.windSafety: High-rise wind and strict fall-protection rules
us-ny.mountingRules: Multifamily fire and façade rules are strict
us-ny.summary: NYC building/fire codes and NEC 690 make multifamily outlet plug-in hard; long interconnect processes add friction.

us-fed.name: Federal-code states (conservative)
us-fed.incentives: Federal ITC 30% mainly tied to rooftop work
us-fed.windSafety: Hurricane/tornado regions: rigid wind ratings (110+ mph)
us-fed.mountingRules: Outlet plug-in treated as illegal wiring / HOA limits
us-fed.summary: Legacy NEC-baseline states. Rapid Shutdown generally bans outlet plug-in; storage off-grid is the only practical path.

nigeria.name: Nigeria
nigeria.baseLoadCoverage: Lights, connectivity, and small appliances during outages
nigeria.antiIslanding: Assumes no grid tie (no reverse flow)
nigeria.meterRequirement: Grid interconnect generally out of scope
nigeria.windSafety: Harmattan dust and outdoor wiring protection
nigeria.mountingRules: Simple roof/courtyard mounts dominate (balcony culture limited)
nigeria.summary: Chronic urban outages drive self-supply; Quadloop-style e-waste battery reuse powers life kits. Counterfeit wiring fire risk is the main hazard.

ethiopia.name: Ethiopia
ethiopia.costRange: Per pump set (grants and loans combined)
ethiopia.baseLoadCoverage: Daytime irrigation and processing powered by solar
ethiopia.incentives: Domestic panel manufacturing and development-aid projects
ethiopia.meterRequirement: No meter premise in unelectrified areas
ethiopia.mountingRules: Ground mounts next to farmland dominate
ethiopia.summary: Solar irrigation (e.g. Dolfano areas) is taking root as productive off-grid power where the grid never arrived.

kenya.name: Kenya
kenya.powerLimit: Life kits to cold-storage warehouse scale
kenya.costRange: Low four-figure JPY kits to warehouse-scale CAPEX
kenya.baseLoadCoverage: Steps from lighting/charging up to agrifood cold storage
kenya.incentives: PayGo, carbon, and development blended finance
kenya.meterRequirement: Grid-tie limited to urban high-tariff avoidance
kenya.windSafety: Equatorial high irradiance and rain-drainage design
kenya.summary: Sun King’s ~7.3M kits and Soulfresh solar cold warehouses jointly address high tariffs and missing cold chain—an advanced market.

za.name: South Africa
za.baseLoadCoverage: Home and shop backup during load-shedding
za.incentives: Municipal SSEG registration and private storage kits
za.antiIslanding: Utility rules apply when SSEG is grid-tied
za.meterRequirement: Grid-tie needs SSEG approval and meter requirements
za.summary: Chronic Eskom load-shedding drives hybrid storage and rooftop/balcony solar in cities. SSEG rules and slow interconnect approvals gate adoption.

rw.name: Rwanda
rw.baseLoadCoverage: Lighting, charging, and small-appliance life power
rw.meterRequirement: Grid interconnect generally out of scope
rw.windSafety: Mountain gust and heavy-rain drainage design
rw.summary: Avoiding mountain grid build-out plus PayGo SHS has spread household solar nationwide. Rural purchasing power and FX risk remain bottlenecks.

tz.name: Tanzania
tz.powerLimit: Community minigrid (kW to tens of kW)
tz.costRange: Operator CAPEX plus customer tariff model
tz.baseLoadCoverage: Day-to-night power for lighting, processing, and water transport
tz.incentives: Private minigrid operators and development finance
tz.antiIslanding: No grid tie / switching risk when the grid arrives
tz.windSafety: Coastal and lakeshore wind / salt protection
tz.mountingRules: Shared community mounts and ground installs dominate
tz.summary: Private community minigrids serve isolated villages and islands. Agri-processing and water-transport self-supply drive demand, but economics and double-investment risk when the grid arrives remain challenges.

ug.name: Uganda
ug.paybackYears: Short felt payback vs. fuel and lighting cost
ug.baseLoadCoverage: Lighting and connectivity charging for daily life
ug.incentives: Private PayGo, humanitarian aid, and development projects
ug.meterRequirement: Grid interconnect generally out of scope
ug.windSafety: Equatorial high irradiance and rain drainage
ug.summary: Beyond the hydro grid, rural areas and refugee settlements adopt lighting kits and autonomous supply. Finance access and last-mile distribution cost remain barriers.

sn.name: Senegal
sn.costRange: Per pump set (shared use with grants)
sn.incentives: ASER rural electrification and development-aid projects
sn.meterRequirement: No meter premise in unelectrified areas
sn.windSafety: Sahel dust and high-temperature panel protection
sn.mountingRules: Ground mounts next to farmland / shared pump stations
sn.summary: Diesel exit and shared solar pumping/irrigation across the Sahel drive adoption. Technician shortages and dust-driven efficiency loss are bottlenecks.

china.name: China
china.meterRequirement: Bidirectional smart meter (direct multifamily plug-in not certified)
china.windSafety: High-rise wind / multi-point fall protection required
china.mountingRules: Property-manager approval is rare; installs behind safety nets
china.summary: The world's largest exporter of balcony PV gear (inverters, batteries). Domestic multifamily pilots are expanding.

japan.name: Japan
japan.procedure: Indoor wiring rules ban outlet plug-in. Self-supply via portable power stations is lawful.
japan.ruleSummary: Indoor wiring rules ban outlet plug-in. Self-supply via portable power stations is lawful.
japan.baseLoadCoverage: Partial self-supply for night appliances / phones via portable storage
japan.meterRequirement: No reverse flow (no direct tie without RPR)
japan.windSafety: Typhoon stow indoors required / strict fall rules
japan.mountingRules: Condo rules often ban railing personal fixtures
japan.summary: Indoor wiring rules ban outlet plug-in. Self-supply via portable power stations is the lawful mainstream path.

au.summary: Addressing tenant solar split in urban apartments, portable plug-in solar adoption is accelerating against soaring grid tariffs.
au.ruleSummary: Guarantees surplus-offset rights for multifamily tenants. Export may be curtailed when the grid is congested.

vn.summary: Following grid curtailment of FIT, urban households rapidly adopt zero-export inverters for self-consumption.

in.summary: Driven by PM-Surya Ghar scheme aiming for 10M homes, compact solar kits thrive against urban load shedding.

sg.summary: Piloting vertical balcony and facade BIPV for high-rise HDB estates under rigorous wind-load and fire standards.

tw.summary: Expanding balcony-mounted disaster resilience systems combining solar with portable power stations for typhoons.

nz.summary: With near 100% smart meter coverage, small-scale surplus is routinely offset on the bill.
nz.ruleSummary: Smart-meter surplus offset is standard. Application steps still differ by lines company.

za-cpt.summary: To overcome loadshedding, the City of Cape Town officially buys excess power from citizens under 'Cash for Power'.

br.summary: Against high tariffs, a small distributed-generation law guarantees household surplus offsets and the market is expanding fast.
br.ruleSummary: Under the small distributed-generation law, surplus power can offset next month’s bill.

until2020.title: Rooftop & FIT Era
until2020.description: Renewables centered on rooftop solar and FIT schemes. Plug-in panels remained a peripheral option.

from2021.title: EU Plug-in PV Expansion
from2021.description: Plug-in panel demand surged across the EU, accelerating debates on safety standards and output caps.

from2023.title: 800W Social Implementation
from2023.description: Germany and the EU clarified ~800W frameworks, enabling social rollout in rental and multifamily housing.

current.title: Global Bifurcation
current.description: World rollout is splitting between jurisdictions advancing legislation and regions leading with off-grid deployment.

movementHistory.title: How balcony solar spread in the West (DIY to law)

guerrilla.title: Germany’s guerrilla grid-tie era
guerrilla.description: Citizen DIY outlet ties clashed with utilities and VDE standards—fueling the “is reverse meter spin illegal?” debate.

energyCrisis.title: Energy crisis & engineering safety proof
energyCrisis.description: Soaring bills sparked mass demand. Engineers showed that 800W stays within wiring thermal safety margins.

euDomino.title: European legalization domino (Solarpaket I / 800W)
euDomino.description: Germany guaranteed balcony install rights in law and temporarily allowed legacy meters. Austria, the UK, and France followed.

usSpread.title: U.S. spillover (120V homes · 1,200W waivers)
usSpread.description: 1,200W kits tuned for high-load 120V/15A homes. Utah and California (SB 868) led state-by-state authorization.

germanyEu.name: Germany & EU
germanyEu.headline: Social rollout of the 800W plug-in solar framework
germanyEu.body: Legal reforms made simple balcony installs a realistic option. Clear output caps and lived-experience messaging are spreading together.

bullets.rentalMultifamily: Lower barriers for rental and multifamily housing

unitedStates.name: United States
unitedStates.headline: State and local institutionalization of plug-in PV
unitedStates.body: Rules are taking shape at the state and municipal level rather than federally. Rental incentives and differentiation from rooftop solar are key themes.

africaDeveloping.name: Africa & developing regions
africaDeveloping.headline: Balcony and facade solar on off-grid and weak grids
africaDeveloping.body: Where the grid is thin or absent, small panels and batteries are daily infrastructure. Modular, no-construction kits are the baseline.

ecosystem.title: Companies, Nonprofits & Ecosystem
ecosystem.lead: A distributed energy ecosystem linking the world and Japan, balcony solar and regional grids

anker-solix-jp.name: Anker Solix (Japan)
anker-solix-jp.subtitle: Plug-in storage & balcony kits
anker-solix-jp.description: Portable power stations and lightweight balcony kits that bring no-construction self-supply into living spaces.

balcony-solar-action-jp.name: Citizen Balcony Solar Network
balcony-solar-action-jp.subtitle: Workshops for multifamily & rental homes
balcony-solar-action-jp.description: A citizen commons practicing balcony solar within building rules and safety codes, with free guides and group purchasing.

seikatsu-club-energy.name: Seikatsu Club Energy
seikatsu-club-energy.subtitle: Co-op renewable purchasing & supply
seikatsu-club-energy.description: Partners with member-funded wind, solar, and biomass sites. Runs a regional surplus-return model via Seikatsu Club Electricity.

digital-grid-jp.name: Digital Grid / DGP
digital-grid-jp.subtitle: Peer-to-peer electricity marketplace
digital-grid-jp.description: Operates a power exchange that directly links producers and consumers with AI and distributed controllers, integrating DERs into markets.

community-power-jp.name: Community Power Japan
community-power-jp.subtitle: Community-led energy independence
community-power-jp.description: A national network of citizen plants and local utilities circulating returns into regional issues and disaster resilience commons.

sekisui-chemical.name: Sekisui Chemical
sekisui-chemical.subtitle: Perovskite solar & lightweight film
sekisui-chemical.description: Scales lightweight, flexible perovskite to expand no-construction capture surfaces onto balconies and walls.

west-holdings.name: West Holdings
west-holdings.subtitle: Central mega-solar & PPA
west-holdings.description: Runs utility-scale solar PPAs dependent on earthworks and racking—a sustaining, dividend-oriented model.

balkonkraftwerk-alliance-eu.name: European Plug-in Solar Alliance
balkonkraftwerk-alliance-eu.subtitle: Socket-ready solar deregulation & adoption
balkonkraftwerk-alliance-eu.description: Citizen–maker coalition that drove Germany’s 800W relief. Advances simplified interconnection and open safety standards.

enphase-energy.name: Enphase Energy
enphase-energy.subtitle: Microinverters & distributed EMS
enphase-energy.description: Per-module control minimizes shade and diffuse-light loss. Forms microgrid foundations that stay autonomous during outages.

rescoop-eu.name: REScoop.eu
rescoop-eu.subtitle: 2,250+ European citizen energy co-ops
rescoop-eu.description: Over 1.5 million citizens jointly own and run renewables, distribution, and efficiency retrofits in the world’s largest energy commons.

layers.heading: Ecosystem composition layers
layers.description: A functional breakdown of the autonomous distributed living VN: product/hardware, regional co-ops/policy, and UX/lived-experience data.

productHardware.title: Product / Hardware
productHardware.description: Design, manufacturing, and distribution of plug-in panels, storage, and inverters.

communityPolicy.title: Regional co-ops / Policy
communityPolicy.description: Cooperative operations, outreach, and incentive or legislative design in the field.

uxLivedData.title: UX / Lived-experience data
uxLivedData.description: UI, metering, and messaging that translate generation into appliance-level value.
